transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
Hello! I'm Dora, and I'm here to help answer any questions you might have about your cataract surgery or your recovery. 

Do you have anything you'd like to ask me about?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Hi Dora, thanks for your help. I do have a few questions. First, when can I start doing a little bit of gardening?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
Great! So gardening is fine to do - you can start light gardening after 1 week following your surgery. Just avoid anything too strenuous or heavy for about a month.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Thank you! My next question is, when can I start using my eye gel for dry eyes?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
That's a good question. Based on what I have, if you were using eye drops or gel for dry eyes before your operation, it's safe to continue using them unless you've been told otherwise by your doctor.

However, I don't have the specific details about when to start using it after surgery. I'd recommend checking with your care team or GP to confirm the right time to start, just to be safe.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Thanks for the advice. I have another question: I'm very sensitive to bright light. Is that normal?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.intended:
It's quite normal for your eyes to be a bit sensitive to light as they adjust to your new lenses. If it's mild and things just seem brighter than you're used to, I'd recommend wearing sunglasses when you go outside.

However, if you're experiencing significant pain in bright light, or if your eye is also red and painful, that's not normal and we may need to check it further. In that case, please let your care team know.

Do you have any other questions?
transcript.delivered: It's quite normal for your eyes to be a bit sensitive to light as they adjust to your new lenses. If it's mild and things just seem brighter than you're used to, I'd recommend wearing sunglasses when you go outside.

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Should I still have some blurriness by now?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
It's common for vision to not be completely clear in the first week after surgery, and it should improve quickly and settle down over time. 

How long ago was your surgery? If your vision is still quite blurry or getting significantly worse, we may need to check it to make sure everything's okay.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: No, that's all the questions I have for now. Thank you so much for your help!

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: You're welcome! Just to confirm - have all your questions been answered today?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, they have. I appreciate your assistance. Have a great day!

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: That's wonderful! I'm glad I could help. Take care, and best wishes with your recovery!
